LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 15.1.1 ORAL REPORTS: EVENTS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.1: Listening and Speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports: Events
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports: Events, part of Strand 15 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How can you make your presentation convincing? 2. Why do we give oral reports?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recount events that take place outside the classroom,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports: Events in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. present a report on occurences taking place out of the classsroom using verbal and non-verbal cues,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports: Events in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the role of oral reports in communication. • Scan through pictures taken in a tourist attraction site and discuss the activities involved, Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech as they are lip read by the teacher or peers • In pairs, search online or offline for oral reports and note the steps taken during the presentations, Control light intensity for learners who are sensitive to light while using the digital devices • In groups, review an out of class activity and order the sequence of events of the activity, • Rehearse an oral report paying attention to verbal and non- verbal cues, 1. How can you make your presentation convincing? 2. Why do we give oral reports? 132 • Present oral reports on the activities as they took place using verbal and non-verbal cues, Learners with manipulation difficulties could use any functional part of the body or use appropriate assistive devices during presentations. • Provide feedback on reports presented by peers and suggest improvements.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 15.1.1 Oral Reports: Events together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination is enhanced as the learner reviews and orders activities taking place outside the classroom.

• Digital literacy enhanced is achieved as the learner interacts with technology while generating ideas from pictures and oral

presentations online.

Values:
Patriotism is fostered the learner is exposed to activities involved in a tourist attraction site.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Environmental Education is promoted as learners scan through pictures taken in a tourist attraction site.

Main points to remember:
